MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  DECEMBER 18, 2023

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  A regular meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 7:05 p.m. at City of Rolling Hills Estates Council Chambers, 4045
  Palos Verdes Dr. N., Rolling Hills Estates, California, by CHAIR BAIN.

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR BAIN led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  Commissioners Present:  Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla, Johnson, Holdsworth
  and Bain

  Commissioners Absent:  McCormick

  City Staff Present:  Assistant City Manager Alexa Davis
  Community Services Supervisor Rosa Pinuelas
  Community Services Coordinator Matt Morrow

  4.  PRESENTATION

  A.  CHANDLER PRESERVE OVERVIEW

  Conservation Director of the Palos Verdes Peninsula Land Conservancy Cris
  Sarabia gave a brief presentation of the projects and activities at the Chandler
  Preserve.

  ACM Davis noted that some plants at City Hall during the turf removal project were
  purchased from the land conservancy.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the sale of the plants from the land
  conservancy. Mr. Sarabia responded that anyone including municipalities and the
  public can purchase the plants on their website and that they also donate any
  surpluses of plants to schools.

  5.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 18, 2023

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
DECEMBER 18, 2023
   CHAIR BAIN requested that on page 7, paragraph 2 line 4 that future years be
  added.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  CIAROLLA to:

  APPROVE THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  SEPTEMBER 18, 2023, WITH THE CORRECTION FROM CHAIR BAIN.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  6.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

  NONE.

  7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  NONE.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  2023 CITY CELEBRATION DEBRIEF

  Coordinator Morrow gave a brief overview of the 2023 City Celebration event (as
  per the agenda material).

  CHAIR BAIN asked if there were any other activities other than the inflatable axe
  throwing activity that appeared to not have been attended well. Coordinator Morrow
  responded that the inflatable axe throwing activity was not as well received as
  expected but noted that the new guided horse rides activity was very well received
  and utilized. COMMISSIONER JOHNSON agreed that the guided horse rides were
  a good addition to the event but mentioned that better signage may assist in more
  people utilizing the activity as it was difficult to find due to its location being away
  from the other activities.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked to confirm that the USC v. UCLA football game
  would not be held on the proposed date of September 14, 2024, for next year’s
  event. Staff noted that they would confirm before finalizing the date.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted that the credit card station continues to work
  well.

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if there was a set budget for this event and about
  the potential extra cost for the proposed extension of the times of some of the

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
DECEMBER 18, 2023
   activities. ACM Davis responded that the City operates on a fiscal year beginning
  July 1, so if there are modifications needed, they would be incorporated in the
  budget preparation for the coming year. She added overall costs of the event
  remain pretty consistent. She also noted that Staff does utilize sponsorships to help
  offset costs but were difficult to attain for this year’s event. Supervisor Pinuelas and
  Coordinator Morrow clarified that the main intention is to keep all the activity times
  consistent with each other instead of off setting times with the activities.
  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that there are some early morning activities for
  young families and that it may be best to end the event at 3pm.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated whether City Council was concerned over
  the overall cost of the City Celebration event. ACM Davis stated that Staff has seen
  the attendance lower around 2pm but that Staff will explore the overall special event
  budget. COMMISSIONER POPE noted that she still does see groups of families
  coming later in the afternoon.

  COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA asked when the event was changed from a Sunday
  to a Saturday. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that the event used to go
  until 9pm in the past, mostly attended by adults, and also included a dinner which
  may be why the day changed as well.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON asked if the prices of the wristbands have changed
  recently. Supervisor Pinuelas responded that the prices were increased two years
  ago but have remained constant since.

  Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the City had a really good year regarding
  sponsorships in 2022 compared to other years including this year. She also noted
  that it was difficult to secure sponsorships with all events this year in response to
  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON suggested that Staff look into the new businesses
  that are beginning to occupy the Promenade PV mall for potential new
  sponsorships. Staff responded that they would look into it.

  The Commission received and filed the report.

  B.  2023 TRACY AUSTIN DOUBLES TENNIS TOURNAMENT DEBRIEF

  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief overview of the 2023 Tracy Austin Doubles
  Tennis Tournament event (as per the agenda material).

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked about the considerations regarding the VIP
  reception that is typically held on Sunday. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that the

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
DECEMBER 18, 2023
   attendance has decreased in the past couple of years with the Sunday afternoon
  reception and Staff is looking into other options.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA noted that this tennis tournament is one of the only
  local tournaments that allows kids to play together with their parents.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that she would be concerned if the VIP reception
  was no longer offered. Supervisor Pinuelas clarified that Staff is not looking to
  remove the reception from the event but looking at other options to help enhance
  the reception for better attendance.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that the t-shirts for this year’s event were very well
  done and looked very nice.

  The Commission received and filed the report.

  C.  2023 PENINSULA HOLIDAY PARADE DEBRIEF

  Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of the 2023 Peninsula Holiday
  Parade event (as per the agenda material).

  CHAIR BAIN expressed her gratitude to Staff for a great event and that it appeared
  to be very well attended.

  COMMISSIONER POPE commended Staff with their work with the new parade
  management company especially with the quick turnaround of this year’s event.

  The Commission received and filed the report.

  D.  2024 PROPOSED SPECIAL EVENT SCHEDULE

  Coordinator Morrow provided a brief overview of the proposed dates of the City’s
  2024 special events (as per the agenda material).

  E.  OVERVIEW OF CITY COMMEMORATION OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLE AND
  JAPANESE AMERICANS OF PALOS VERDES PENINSULA

  ACM Davis provided a brief overview of the city commemoration of indigenous
  people and Japanese Americans of Palos Verdes Peninsula (as per the agenda
  material).

  ACM Davis stated that Staff’s initial plan is for these items to be completed in the
  next two to three years in response to CHAIR BAIN.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
DECEMBER 18, 2023
   The Commission received and filed the report.

  F.  OVERVIEW OF PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION LARGE DONOR FUNDRAISING
  CAMPAIGN FOR NATURE CENTER PROJECT AND ASSOCIATED NAMING
  POLICY

  ACM Davis provided a brief overview of the Pepper Tree Foundation large donor
  fundraising campaign for the Nature Center project and the associated naming
  policy (as per the agenda material).

  In response to CHAIR BAIN, ACM Davis stated that the Fundraising Committee
  and City Council thoroughly discussed the duration of the naming and that it was
  determined that most people would have the expectation that their name will always
  remain attached to their specific donation. COMMISSIONER POPE also stated that
  it was discussed that there were limits to the corporate level of naming rights to the
  Nature Center project also in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  ACM Davis noted that Staff would be coming back with a donation program for
  donations less than $25,000 in the future in response to CHAIR BAIN.

  In response to CHAIR BAIN, ACM Davis provided an overview of the Fundraising
  Committee with members appointed by the Pepper Tree Foundation Board/City
  Council and COMMISSIONER POPE added that members include a mix of
  fundraising professionals and volunteers at the community level who have an
  overall sense of best practices and personal experiences in fundraising with capital
  projects.

  COMMISSIONER POPE stated that there were discussions among the committee
  regarding the removal of naming rights, if necessary, in response to
  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON.

  G.  JANUARY AND FEBRUARY MEETING DATES (VERBAL REPORT)

  Supervisor Pinuelas informed the Commission that the January and February
  meeting dates fall on City observed holidays and recommended that the regular
  meetings be cancelled, and special meetings be scheduled on the following
  Tuesdays for January and February. The Commission had no concerns and
  approved the special meetings for the January and February meetings.

  H.  CONSIDERATION OF COMMISSION MEETING DAY CHANGE

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
DECEMBER 18, 2023
   Supervisor Pinuelas provided a brief overview of a consideration and the process
  to change the Park and Activities Commission’s regular meeting day from the third
  Monday to the third Tuesday of the month (as per the agenda material).

  Supervisor Pinuelas noted that the City Council meetings are currently scheduled
  for the second and fourth Tuesdays of the month in response to COMMISSIONER
  CIAROLLA.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that when the Park and Activities
  Commission meetings were previously scheduled on Tuesdays and a conflict
  occurred with a Council meeting the Commission meetings were still held on the
  Tuesday but in City Hall instead of Council Chambers.

  ACM Davis noted that it would be rare that there would be a Council meeting held
  on the third Tuesday of the month that would cause a conflict for staff in attending
  both meetings as it would require an extra Council meeting being scheduled in
  response to COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH.

  COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA stated that the Commission meetings were
  changed from Tuesdays to Mondays due to the Commission at the time having
  difficulties in meeting on Tuesdays in response to COMMISSIONER POPE.

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER
  PERSICHINA to:

  RECOMMEND TO COUNCIL THAT THE PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  COMMISSION MEETINGS BE CHANGED FROM THE THIRD MONDAY
  TO THE THIRD TUESDAY OF THE MONTH.

  There being no objection, CHAIR BAIN so ordered.

  I.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  NONE

  9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER HOLDSWORTH reported that the playground at Rockbluff Park
  has been fully completed with the installation of the water fountain and there were
  no issues reported.

  COMMISSIONER JOHNSON reported that there were no concerns with
  Dapplegray Park.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
DECEMBER 18, 2023
   COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA reported that Ernie Howlett Park turf restoration
  project that began in July looks great.

  CHAIR BAIN reported that weeds are beginning to overtake the new rock area of
  Highridge Park and that there is a large accumulation of pine needles throughout
  the trail areas as well. Staff stated that they would connect with the landscaping
  contractor to investigate and clean up as needed. She also reported that the trash
  cans are consistently overflowing at the park. COMMISSIONER POPE noted that
  the trash cans behind the softball field are also overflowing. CHAIR BAIN reported
  that there still appears to be off leash dogs at the park and suggested some
  additional signage informing park patrons that dogs must be leashed while at the
  park. COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA asked how the City’s code enforcement
  could enforce these issues with off leash dogs at the park. ACM Davis stated that
  he can issue fines but there is a process to follow and typically it is more education
  than enforcement.

  B.  MATTERS OF INTEREST (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER POPE asked if the City has considered creating a specific dog
  park area somewhere in the City. Supervisor Pinuelas stated that Staff can look into
  this item if the Commission deems necessary. The Commission requested that a
  dog park item be added as a future agenda item.

  CHAIR BAIN informed and updated the Commission about the Nature Center item
  discussed at the December 12, 2023, City Council meeting that she attended.

  10.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF SEPTEMBER 12, 2023
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  B.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF SEPTEMBER 26, 2023
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  C.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF OCTOBER 10, 2023
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  D.  CITY COUNCIL ACTION OF NOVEMBER 14, 2023
  RECEIVED AND FILED.

  11.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  SECURITY CAMERA PROJECT UPDATE

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  7
DECEMBER 18, 2023
   NONE

  B.  PUBLIC OUTREACH-JANUARY

  NONE

  12.  ADJOURNMENT

  CHAIR BAIN ADJOURNED THE MEETING AT 8:26 PM TO THE NEXT PARK AND
  ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING ON JANUARY 16, 2024, AT 7:00 P.M.,
  WHICH WILL BE HELD AT CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CITY HALL.

  There being no objection, so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  ___________________________

  Community Services Coordinator  Chair, Park & Activities Commission
